# Test Fact Pack — Bramble County (fictional)

Used with every fixture so that test runs are comparable. **Bramble County does not exist.** Every
place, agency, and organization below is invented. Nothing here describes a real jurisdiction.

Replace this with the real [county fact pack](../../../context/county-fact-pack.md) for live use.

---

## 1. Basics

- County: Bramble County, State of Weldon
- County seat: Delphi Springs
- Population: approximately 8,400 (2024 estimate)
- Land area: approximately 610 square miles
- Incorporated towns: Delphi Springs (2,900), Kettle Ford (1,100), Ashgrove (480)
- Unincorporated communities: Mill Bend, Two Creeks, Harlow Corner
- Adjacent counties: Verlin, Naught, Pierce Hollow
- Time zone: Central, observes daylight saving time

## 2. Geography and infrastructure

- Highways: US 61 north–south through Delphi Springs; State Route 42 east–west; County Road 9
  serving Mill Bend
- Waterways: Wicket River, Sawyer Creek, Two Creeks Branch
- Gauges used by this office: Wicket River at Kettle Ford (flood stage 18 feet); Sawyer Creek at
  Ashgrove (flood stage 11 feet)
- Rail: one freight line crossing State Route 42 at grade in Kettle Ford
- Airstrip: Bramble County Airfield, grass, no tower
- Terrain: river bottomland north of Kettle Ford, ridge roads south of Ashgrove
- Single-access areas: Mill Bend, reached only by County Road 9, which crosses Sawyer Creek at a
  low-water bridge

## 3. Hazards

| Hazard | Season | Typical local impact |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Flash and riverine flooding | Spring, early summer | County Road 9 low-water bridge overtops; bottomland farms |
| Severe thunderstorms and tornadoes | Spring | Power loss, tree blockage, occasional structure damage |
| Ice storms | December to February | Multi-day outages, roads impassable, long restoration |
| Extreme heat | July, August | Outdoor workers, older residents without air conditioning |
| Grass and field fires | Late summer, fall | Volunteer department strain, smoke on US 61 |
| Hazardous materials in transit | Year-round | Rail crossing and US 61 truck traffic |

## 4. Organization

- Staffing: one full-time Emergency Manager, one part-time deputy at 20 hours per week
- EOC: conference room at the county courthouse annex, generator-backed
- Activation levels: Level 3 monitoring, Level 2 partial, Level 1 full
- Local emergency declaration: County Commission Chair
- Public messaging authority: Emergency Manager

## 5. Response resources

- Fire: four departments, all volunteer, roughly 60 members countywide
- EMS: one county service, two ambulances, one staffed 24 hours and one on call
- Law enforcement: Sheriff's Office with 9 deputies; Delphi Springs Police with 4 officers
- Dispatch: county 911 center, two dispatchers on day shift and one overnight
- Road department: 11 employees, 6 plow trucks, 2 graders
- Hospital: none in county. Nearest is Verlin Regional, 38 minutes from Delphi Springs
- Public health: Bramble County Health Department, 5 staff
- Volunteers: CERT team of about 15, activity varies; amateur radio group of about 8

## 6. Facilities used in emergencies

| Facility | Type | Typical role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Bramble County High School | School | Primary shelter, generator, commercial kitchen |
| Delphi Springs Community Center | Community center | Warming and cooling center, no generator |
| Kettle Ford Methodist Church | Church | Secondary shelter, roughly 60 capacity |
| Bramble County Fairgrounds | Fairgrounds | Staging, livestock, points of distribution |

## 7. Warning and information channels

- Mass notification: BrambleAlert, 160-character limit
- Sirens: Delphi Springs and Kettle Ford only; no rural coverage
- Website: brambleco.example.gov
- Social media: Facebook page "Bramble County Emergency Management"
- Radio: WBRM 1340 AM, WKFD 98.3 FM
- Newspaper: Bramble County Record, weekly, Thursdays
- Television: Verlin market stations, 50 miles away
- Public contact: 555-0100, published main office line
- Public information authority: Emergency Manager; no dedicated PIO

## 8. Population considerations

- Roughly 24 percent of residents are over 65
- Two long-term care facilities, both in Delphi Springs, roughly 110 beds combined
- About 40 households are known in aggregate to depend on electrically powered medical equipment
- Cell coverage is unreliable south of Ashgrove and in the Mill Bend bottoms
- Roughly 15 percent of households have no vehicle available during the workday
- Substantial farm population; cattle and row crop operations countywide
- Population rises sharply during fair week in August and deer season in November

## 9. Agriculture and economy

- Crops: corn, soybeans, hay
- Livestock: cattle, two dairies, one poultry operation
- Grain elevator in Kettle Ford near the rail crossing
- Major employers: school district, county government, Ridgeline Foods packing plant (about 180
  employees), Verlin Regional Hospital commuters
- Two facilities report hazardous materials under state requirements

## 10. Mutual aid and partners

- Countywide fire mutual aid agreement; regional agreements with Verlin and Naught counties
- State Emergency Management District 4
- Red Cross regional chapter, 60 miles away, typical arrival 4 to 6 hours
- Bramble County Ministerial Association coordinates church volunteers

## 11. Standing constraints

- No dedicated PIO. The Emergency Manager writes all public messaging.
- Fire response is entirely volunteer and thins sharply on weekday mornings.
- No in-house GIS staff.
- Overtime beyond 16 hours per employee per event requires County Commission approval.
- Shelter operations depend on the school district and the Ministerial Association.
- The Mill Bend low-water bridge is the county's single most common isolation point.
- Only one ambulance is staffed overnight.

## 12. Language for the model

```text
Do not invent road closures, shelter openings, gauge readings, outage counts, casualty
figures, damage estimates, or activation decisions. If a fact is not in this pack or in
the inputs I provide, write UNKNOWN and list it under Information Needed. Assume rural
constraints: volunteer response, long travel distances, and limited staffing.
```
